# 0 Packages check

This section ensures that all required R packages are available for the analysis and interactive modules in this project.

```{r}
packages <- c(
  "shiny", "shinydashboard",
  "jsonlite", "igraph", "ggraph",
  "dplyr", "lubridate",
  "plotly", "visNetwork", "DT",
  "leaflet", "ggridges", "ggmosaic"
)
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for (pkg in packages) {
  if (!pkg %in% installed) install.packages(pkg)
  library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}
```

# 1 Data Preparation & Testing

We load your knowledge‐graph JSON, clean it into tidy node and edge tables, and build an igraph for global metrics.

```{r}
library(jsonlite)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(igraph)

# Load JSON
raw_json <- fromJSON("MC1_graph.json")

# Helper: Parse "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM-DD"
parse_date <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x[x == ""] <- NA
  year_only <- !is.na(x) & grepl("^\\d{4}$", x)
  x[year_only] <- paste0(x[year_only], "-01-01")
  ymd(x)
}

# Clean nodes
g_nodes_df <- as_tibble(raw_json$nodes) %>%
  rename(
    id        = id,
    label     = name,
    node_type = `Node Type`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    id           = as.character(id),
    release_date = parse_date(release_date),
    written_date = if ("written_date" %in% names(.)) parse_date(written_date) else as.Date(NA)
  )

# Clean edges
g_edges_df <- as_tibble(raw_json$links) %>%
  rename(
    from_id  = source,
    to_id    = target,
    relation = `Edge Type`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    from_id = as.character(from_id),
    to_id   = as.character(to_id)
  )

# Build igraph
g_all <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = g_edges_df %>%
    transmute(from = from_id, to = to_id, relation),
  vertices = g_nodes_df %>%
    transmute(name = id, label, node_type),
  directed = TRUE
)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(
  nrow(g_nodes_df) > 0,
  nrow(g_edges_df) > 0,
  all(c("id", "label", "node_type") %in% names(g_nodes_df)),
  all(c("from_id", "to_id", "relation") %in% names(g_edges_df))
)

print(g_all)
```

# 2 Module 1: Influence Over Time

Tasks & Questions:

-   Who has Sailor been most influenced by over time?

-   Was influence intermittent or gradual?

## 2.1 Input & Output Definitions

| Input ID | Widget | Choices / Default | Purpose |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `yearRange` | sliderInput | 2010–2040; default c(2010,2040) | Filter by written_date year |
| `artist1` | selectInput | `nodes_df$name`; default “Sailor Shift” | Choose focal artist |

| Output ID | Render         | Description                 |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| `tsPlot`  | renderPlotly() | Line chart: count per year  |
| `tsTable` | renderDT()     | Data table of yearly counts |

## 2.2 Code Preparation & Testing

Before wiring up the Shiny module, we encapsulate our data-manipulation steps into a reusable function and verify its basic behavior:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)

g      <- fromJSON("MC1_graph.json")
nodes  <- g$nodes
edges  <- g$links

get_influence_over_time <- function(
  artist_name,
  yearRange = c(2010, 2040),
  nodes_df   = nodes,
  edges_df   = edges
) {
  # 1. Find the artist’s Person‐node ID
  artist_id <- nodes_df %>%
    filter(`Node Type` == "Person", name == artist_name) %>%
    pull(id)
  if (length(artist_id) == 0) {
    stop("Artist not found: ", artist_name)
  }

  # 2. Get all the Song IDs they perform
  artist_songs <- edges_df %>%
    filter(`Edge Type` == "PerformerOf", source == artist_id) %>%
    pull(target)
  if (length(artist_songs) == 0) {
    warning("No songs found for artist: ", artist_name)
  }

  # 3. Build the influence‐edges table (one row per Sailor song → influencer)
  wanted_types <- c(
    "InStyleOf", "LyricalReferenceTo",
    "InterpolatesFrom", "DirectlySamples", "CoverOf"
  )

  infl_edges <- edges_df %>%
    filter(
      `Edge Type` %in% wanted_types,
      source         %in% artist_songs
    ) %>%
    transmute(
      song_id   = source,           # Sailor’s song
      infl_song = target,           # the influencing song
      rel_type  = `Edge Type`
    ) %>%
    # 3a. bring in the Sailor‐song’s release year
    left_join(
      nodes_df %>%
        filter(`Node Type` == "Song") %>%
        transmute(song_id = id,
                  year    = as.integer(substr(release_date, 1, 4))),
      by = "song_id"
    ) %>%
    # 3b. bring in the Person‐node who performed the influencing song
    left_join(
      edges_df %>%
        filter(`Edge Type` == "PerformerOf") %>%
        transmute(infl_song = target,
                  performer = source),
      by = "infl_song"
    ) %>%
    # 3c. bring in the influencer’s name
    left_join(
      nodes_df %>%
        filter(`Node Type` == "Person") %>%
        transmute(performer  = id,
                  influencer = name),
      by = "performer"
    ) %>%
    # 3d. drop any incomplete rows
    filter(!is.na(influencer), !is.na(year))

  # 4. Count by year
  counts <- infl_edges %>%
    count(year, name = "num_influences")

  # 5. Fill zero‐counts for the full slider window
  full_years <- tibble(year = seq(yearRange[1], yearRange[2]))
  full_years %>%
    left_join(counts, by = "year") %>%
    replace_na(list(num_influences = 0)) %>%
    arrange(year)
}
```

Now we test also Sailor Shift case:

```{r}

# gives you a 31‐row tibble for 2010–2040
df_sailor <- get_influence_over_time("Sailor Shift", c(2010, 2040))
print(df_sailor)

```

### Code for UI Dashboard

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# Assume these are already in your global environment:
# • nodes       – your g_nodes_df or similar with Person nodes
# • edges_labeled – your preprocessed edge table with to_written_date
# • get_influence_over_time() – the helper that returns a tibble (year, num_influences)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Influence Over Time"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput(
        inputId = "yearRange",
        label   = "Year range:",
        min     = 2010,
        max     = 2040,
        value   = c(2010, 2040),
        sep     = "",
        step    = 1
      ),

      selectizeInput(
        inputId  = "artist1",
        label    = "Choose artist:",
        choices  = NULL,            # will be populated server-side
        options  = list(
          placeholder = 'Type to search…',
          maxOptions  = 5000
        )
      )
    ),

    mainPanel(
      plotlyOutput("tsPlot"),
      br(),
      DTOutput("tsTable")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Prepare the list of artists once
  artist_choices <- sort(
    unique(
      nodes %>%
        filter(`Node Type` == "Person") %>%
        pull(name)
    )
  )

  # Populate the selectize input server-side
  updateSelectizeInput(
    session,
    "artist1",
    choices = artist_choices,
    server  = TRUE
  )

  # Reactive data frame of influence counts
  influence_df <- reactive({
    req(input$artist1, input$yearRange)
    get_influence_over_time(
      artist     = input$artist1,
      yearRange  = input$yearRange
    )
  })

  # Render the time‐series plot
  output$tsPlot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- influence_df()
    plot_ly(
      df,
      x    = ~year,
      y    = ~num_influences,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "lines+markers",
      hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y} influences<extra></extra>"
    ) %>%
      layout(
        title = paste("Influence over time for", input$artist1),
        xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
        yaxis = list(title = "Number of influences")
      )
  })

  # Render the data table
  output$tsTable <- renderDT({
    df <- influence_df()
    datatable(
      df,
      rownames = FALSE,
      options = list(
        pageLength   = 10,
        lengthChange = FALSE,
        autoWidth    = TRUE
      )
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

# 3 Module 2: Collaboration Network & Propagation

Tasks & Questions:

-   Who has Sailor collaborated with, and whom has she influenced (directly/indirectly)?

-   How has influence propagate through her songs and collaborators?

## 3.1 Input & Output Definitions

| Input ID | Widget | Choices / Default | Purpose |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `artist2` | selectInput | `nodes_df$label`; default “Sailor Shift” | Choose the focal artist for the network |
| `relationTypes` | checkboxGroupInput | c("CollaboratorOf", "InfluencedBy") | Select which edge types to include (collaborations vs. influences) |
| `networkDepth` | sliderInput | 1–3; default 1 | How many hops (degrees of separation) to traverse from the focal artist |

| Output ID | Render | Description |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `networkPlot` | renderPlotly() | Interactive network graph showing nodes and edges for the selected artist |
| `propTable` | renderDT() | Data table listing each connected node, relation type, and shortest path |

## 3.2 Code Preparation & Testing

This section defines how the filtered ego-network is built from the full graph g_all, and how the propagation paths are traced through shortest path calculations:

```{r}
library(igraph)

# — 1. Build a filtered ego‐network around the chosen artist —————————————
get_collab_influence_graph <- function(artist = "Sailor Shift",
                                       rel_types = NULL,
                                       depth     = 3) {
  # If no rel_types given, include every edge relation in the graph
  if (is.null(rel_types)) {
    rel_types <- E(g_all)$relation %>% unique()
  }
  
  # 1a) Keep only edges of the selected types
  g_filt <- subgraph.edges(
    g_all,
    E(g_all)[ E(g_all)$relation %in% rel_types ],
    delete.vertices = FALSE
  )
  
  # 1b) Find the vertex index of the focal artist
  vid <- which(V(g_filt)$label == artist)
  if (length(vid) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Artist '%s' not found in the graph.", artist))
  }
  
  # 1c) Gather all vertices within `depth` hops
  vs <- ego(
    graph = g_filt,
    order = depth,
    nodes = vid,
    mode  = "all"
  )[[1]]
  
  # 1d) Return the induced subgraph
  induced_subgraph(g_filt, vids = vs)
}

# — 2. Build propagation paths table ———————————————————————————————
get_propagation_table <- function(sub_g, artist = "Sailor Shift") {
  # Locate the starting vertex
  vid <- which(V(sub_g)$label == artist)
  if (length(vid) == 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Artist '%s' not in the subgraph.", artist))
  }
  
  # Compute shortest paths from the artist to every node
  paths <- shortest_paths(
    graph = sub_g,
    from  = vid,
    to    = V(sub_g),
    mode  = "all"
  )$vpath
  
  # Build a tibble: target, path length, and the full path string
  tibble::tibble(
    target      = sapply(paths, function(p) V(sub_g)$label[tail(p,1)]),
    path_length = sapply(paths, length) - 1,
    path        = sapply(paths, function(p)
                      paste(V(sub_g)$label[p], collapse = " → "))
  )
}
```

Let's test the function:

```{r}
# 1. Extract the full ego‐network for Sailor Shift using every relation
full_graph_ss <- get_collab_influence_graph(
  artist    = "Sailor Shift",
  rel_types = NULL,
  depth     = 3
)
print(full_graph_ss)

# 2. Propagation table for Sailor Shift
prop_table_ss <- get_propagation_table(full_graph_ss, artist = "Sailor Shift")
print(prop_table_ss)

# 3. And for another artist, say “Maya Jensen”
full_graph_mj <- get_collab_influence_graph(
  artist    = "Maya Jensen",
  rel_types = NULL,
  depth     = 2
)
prop_table_mj <- get_propagation_table(full_graph_mj, artist = "Maya Jensen")
print(full_graph_mj)
print(prop_table_mj)
```

### Left Sidebar – User Controls

### Code for UI Dashboard

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(visNetwork)
library(igraph)    # ← make sure this is loaded
library(DT)
library(dplyr)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # 1) populate artist list
  updateSelectizeInput(
    session, "artist",
    choices = sort(V(g_all)$label),
    server  = TRUE
  )

  # 2) filtered ego‐network
  subgraph <- reactive({
    req(input$artist)
    get_collab_influence_graph(
      artist    = input$artist,
      rel_types = input$rel_types,
      depth     = input$depth
    )
  })

  # 3) *** FIXED *** visNetwork data  
  vis_data <- reactive({
    sg <- subgraph()

    # 3a) vertices → data.frame
    verts <- igraph::as_data_frame(sg, what = "vertices")
    nodes_df <- verts %>%
      rename(
        id    = name,       # igraph stores node IDs in ‘name’
        title = label       # human‐readable label
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        group = node_type   # use your node_type attr for coloring
      )

    # 3b) edges → data.frame
    eds <- igraph::as_data_frame(sg, what = "edges")
    edges_df <- eds %>%
      rename(
        from  = from,      # source vertex id
        to    = to,        # target vertex id
        title = relation   # use the relation as the hover text
      )

    list(nodes = nodes_df, edges = edges_df)
  })

  # 4) render the network
  output$networkGraph <- renderVisNetwork({
    d <- vis_data()
    visNetwork(d$nodes, d$edges) %>%
      visOptions(
        highlightNearest = list(enabled = TRUE, degree = 1),
        nodesIdSelection = TRUE
      ) %>%
      visLegend() %>%
      visLayout(randomSeed = 42)
  })

  # 5) propagation table
  output$propagationTable <- renderDT({
    sg <- subgraph()
    df <- get_propagation_table(sg, input$artist)
    datatable(
      df,
      rownames = FALSE,
      options  = list(pageLength = 10, lengthChange = FALSE, autoWidth = TRUE)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

# 4 Module 3: Genre-Level Influence Patterns

Tasks & Questions:

-   Which genres and top artists have been most influenced by Oceanus Folk?

-   Which genres or artists has Oceanus Folk drawn inspiration from?

## 4.1 Input & Output Definitions

| Input ID | Widget | Choices / Default | Purpose |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `genre_focus` | selectInput | Genre list; default = Oceanus Folk | Choose the genre to analyze (starting with Oceanus Folk) |
| `influenceDir` | radioButtons | `c("From", "To")` | Direction of influence: from genre to others, or others to this genre |
| `topN` | numericInput | default = 10 | Limit number of top genres/artists shown in bar chart & table |

| Output ID | Render | Description |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `genreBarPlot` | renderPlotly() | Horizontal bar plot of top genres/artists influenced or influencing |
| `genreTable` | renderDT() | Data table showing genre interactions: target, count, and example artists |

## 4.2 Code Preparation & Testing

We’ll use edge metadata (like Edge Type = InfluencedBy) and node genres to build an influence matrix between genres. Here’s a proposed structure for this:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

edges_labeled <- g_edges_df %>%
  # join the song info on to_id → id
  left_join(
    g_nodes_df %>%
      select(id, label, release_date) %>%
      rename(
        to_label        = label,
        to_release_date = release_date
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        to_release_date = ymd(to_release_date)
      ),
    by = c("to_id" = "id")
  )

# 1) Filter only influence‐type edges
influence_edges <- edges_labeled %>%
  filter(relation %in% c(
    "InStyleOf", "LyricalReferenceTo",
    "InterpolatesFrom", "DirectlySamples", "CoverOf"
  ))

# 2) Attach genres for source and target nodes
infl_ext <- influence_edges %>%
  left_join(
    g_nodes_df %>% select(id, genre) %>% rename(source_genre = genre),
    by = c("from_id" = "id")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    g_nodes_df %>% select(id, genre) %>% rename(target_genre = genre),
    by = c("to_id" = "id")
  )

# 3) Compute summary by focus_genre and direction
get_genre_influence_data <- function(
  focus_genre = "Oceanus Folk",
  direction   = "From",
  topN        = 10
) {
  # Choose source vs. target based on direction
  if (direction == "From") {
    df <- infl_ext %>% filter(source_genre == focus_genre)
    group_col <- sym("target_genre")
    artist_col <- sym("to_id")
  } else {
    df <- infl_ext %>% filter(target_genre == focus_genre)
    group_col <- sym("source_genre")
    artist_col <- sym("from_id")
  }
  
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!group_col)) %>%
    group_by(genre = !!group_col) %>%
    summarise(
      influence_count = n(),
      example_artists = paste(
        unique(g_nodes_df$label[match(!!artist_col, g_nodes_df$id)])[1:5],
        collapse = "; "
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(influence_count)) %>%
    slice_head(n = topN)
}

# 4) Sanity check
test_from <- get_genre_influence_data("Oceanus Folk", "From", 5)
stopifnot(
  nrow(test_from) <= 5,
  all(c("genre", "influence_count", "example_artists") %in% names(test_from))
)

print(test_from)
```

## 4.3 UI Storyboard

### Sidebar – User Controls (Inputs)

| UI Element | Type | Description |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Genre Selector** | `selectInput` | Dropdown list of all genres (default: Oceanus Folk). Allows the user to pick a genre as the focal point for analysis. |
| **Direction Radio** | `radioButtons` | Two choices: “From” (genres/artists influenced by selected genre), “To” (genres/artists that influence selected genre). |
| **Top N Numeric** | `numericInput` | User sets the number (N) of top genres/artists to show in the outputs (default 10, min 1, max 30). |

### Main Panel – Outputs

| UI Element | Type | Description |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Genre Bar Plot** | `renderPlotly()` | Interactive horizontal bar chart: shows the top N genres (and, optionally, key artists) most influenced by or influencing the focal genre. |
| **Genre Table** | `renderDT()` | Data table: shows detailed genre-genre links (genre name, influence count, and example artists), sortable and searchable. |

![](image3.png)

::: callout-note
User flow:

1.  User opens the module. By default, Oceanus Folk is selected as the focal genre, “From” direction is chosen, and the top 10 results are displayed.
2.  User changes the genre to “Electro Pop.” The bar plot and table instantly update to show genres influenced by Electro Pop (or that influence Electro Pop, depending on direction).
3.  User toggles direction from “From” to “To,” revealing genres that have influenced the currently selected genre.
4.  User adjusts the Top N to 20, revealing more connections in both the bar plot and the data table.
5.  User explores the bar plot, hovering over bars to view example artists.
6.  User scans/sorts the table, quickly identifying which genres and artists are most involved in cross-genre influence with the selected focal genre.
:::

### Code for UI Dashboard

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

# Assumes you have in your global environment:
# • g_nodes_df: a data frame with columns `id`, `genre`, `label`, etc.
# • get_genre_influence_data(): the function you defined above

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Genre-Level Influence Patterns"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      # 1. Genre selector (server‐side selectize for performance)
      selectizeInput(
        inputId  = "genre_focus",
        label    = "Focal genre:",
        choices  = NULL,    # populated in server
        options  = list(
          placeholder = "Type to search…",
          maxOptions  = 5000
        )
      ),
      
      # 2. Direction toggle
      radioButtons(
        inputId  = "influenceDir",
        label    = "Direction of influence:",
        choices  = c("From selected genre" = "From",
                     "To selected genre"   = "To"),
        selected = "From"
      ),
      
      # 3. Top N control
      numericInput(
        inputId = "topN",
        label   = "Top N genres/artists:",
        value   = 10,
        min     = 1,
        max     = 50,
        step    = 1
      )
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      # 4. Bar chart output
      plotlyOutput("genreBarPlot", height = "400px"),
      br(),
      # 5. Data table output
      DTOutput("genreTable")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Populate the genre list server-side
  updateSelectizeInput(
    session, "genre_focus",
    choices = sort(unique(g_nodes_df$genre)),
    server  = TRUE
  )
  
  # Reactive summary table based on inputs
  summary_tbl <- reactive({
    req(input$genre_focus, input$influenceDir, input$topN)
    get_genre_influence_data(
      focus_genre = input$genre_focus,
      direction   = input$influenceDir,
      topN        = input$topN
    )
  })
  
  # Render the horizontal bar chart
  output$genreBarPlot <- renderPlotly({
    df <- summary_tbl()
    plot_ly(
      df,
      x = ~influence_count,
      y = ~reorder(genre, influence_count),
      type = "bar",
      orientation = "h",
      hovertemplate = paste(
        "<b>%{y}</b><br>",
        "Count: %{x}<br>",
        "Examples: %{customdata}",
        "<extra></extra>"
      ),
      customdata = ~example_artists
    ) %>%
      layout(
        title = if (input$influenceDir == "From") {
          paste("Top", input$topN, "genres influenced by", input$genre_focus)
        } else {
          paste("Top", input$topN, "genres influencing", input$genre_focus)
        },
        xaxis = list(title = "Influence edges"),
        yaxis = list(title = "")
      )
  })
  
  # Render the data table
  output$genreTable <- renderDT({
    df <- summary_tbl() %>%
      rename(
        Genre            = genre,
        `Influence Count`= influence_count,
        `Example Artists`= example_artists
      )
    datatable(
      df,
      rownames = FALSE,
      options = list(
        pageLength = input$topN,
        lengthChange = FALSE,
        autoWidth = TRUE
      )
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
